text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Agriculture and Rural Development Ministry expects coffee output of 250,000-260,000 tonnes in 1997.
-- China's Deputy Culture Minister Fan Zhenwu arrived in Hanoi for a four-day visit to boost cultural exchanges between Vietnam and China.
-- Vietnam's Education and Training Minister Tran Hong Quan said the government was encouraging foreign investors and universities to invest in the country's education system.
-- Vietnam's National Assembly will begin a one-month session on April 2. Seven bills, including commercial and banking bills, are expected to be passed into law.

-- The Asian Development Bank has pledged loans of $1.4-1.5 billion and technical assistance worth $27.5 million to Vietnam in the next three years, but raised concerns over slow disbursement of the funds.
-- Vietnam expects to export more than 2.5 million tonnes of rice between March and September.
-- Vietnam plans to import 1.5 tonnes of fertilizer in 1997.
